You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To identify a british shorthair cat, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Observe the density of the coat (2 minutes)
Step 2. Note the roundness of the whisker pads (1 minute)
Step 3. Check for a thick, muscular neck (30 seconds)
Step 4. Examine the width of the chest (45 seconds)
Step 5. Evaluate the overall "cobby" body type (2 minutes)
Step 6. Look for a broad, round head shape (1 minute)
Step 7. Feel the texture of the fur for a "crisp" quality (1 minute)
Step 8. Check for a short, thick tail with a rounded tip (30 seconds)
Step 9. Compare the cat to a breed standard photo (5 minutes)
Step 10. Inspect the chin for firm development (1 minute)
Step 11. Observe the spacing between the ears (1 minute)
Step 12. Look for the characteristic "smile" expression (2 minutes)
Step 13. Measure the length of the legs relative to the body (3 minutes)
Step 14. Confirm the absence of a nose "stop" or break (1 minute)
Step 15. Verify the eye color matches the coat color (1 minute)
Step 16. Assess the thickness of the ear leather (30 seconds)
Step 17. Examine the roundness of the paws (1 minute)
Step 18. Check for a plush, double-layered undercoat (2 minutes)
Step 19. Identify the specific shade of "blue" or other color (5 minutes)
Step 20. Look for the short, straight nose (1 minute)
Step 21. Observe the cat's profile from the side (2 minutes)
Step 22. Note the medium-to-large size of the cat (1 minute)
Step 23. Check the density of the fur on the hindquarters (1 minute)
Step 24. Verify the tail is in proportion to the body (1 minute)
Step 25. Inspect the bridge of the nose (30 seconds)
Step 26. Evaluate the bone structure of the legs (2 minutes)
Step 27. Examine the size of the feet (45 seconds)
Step 28. Look for the wide-set placement of the eyes (1 minute)
Step 29. Check for a level back (30 seconds)
Step 30. Observe the cat's gait and movement (3 minutes)
Step 31. Document the eye shape as large and round (2 minutes)
Step 32. Review the cat's pedigree papers if available (1 hour)
Step 33. Check for the absence of a "ruff" around the neck (1 minute)
Step 34. Record the final physical measurements (10 minutes)
Step 35. Consult with a breed expert (30 minutes)
Step 36. Note the rounded tips of the ears (30 seconds)
Step 37. Inspect the forehead for a slight curve (1 minute)
Step 38. Photograph the cat from multiple angles (15 minutes)
Step 39. Observe the cat in a relaxed state (10 minutes)
Step 40. Look for the lack of any "fluffiness" in the tail (1 minute)
Step 41. Examine the density of the coat on the chest (1 minute)
Step 42. Check for the "teddy bear" appearance (2 minutes)
Step 43. Verify the ears are small to medium in size (30 seconds)
Step 44. Observe the cat's temperament (20 minutes)
Step 45. Research the common traits of the British Shorthair (1 hour)
Step 46. Check the width of the muzzle (1 minute)
Step 47. Observe the roundness of the cheeks (1 minute)
Step 48. Summarize the physical findings (15 minutes)
Step 49. Check for a slight break at the bridge of the nose (1 minute)
Step 50. Compare the cat to a Scottish Straight for differences (15 minutes)
Step 51. Look for the lack of a pointed pattern (2 minutes)
Step 52. Observe the cat's profile for a "brick-like" shape (1 minute)
Step 53. Note the copper or gold eye color (30 seconds)
Step 54. Verify the weight of the cat (2 minutes)
Step 55. Search for regional breed variations (45 minutes)
Step 56. Inspect the tail for any kinks (1 minute)
Step 57. Check the fur length on the belly (1 minute)
Step 58. Observe the cat's stance (2 minutes)
Step 59. Look for the absence of any white lockets or spots (2 minutes)
Step 60. Finalize the breed identification report (20 minutes)
Step 61. Measure the distance between the eyes (1 minute)
Step 62. Check for the presence of a "frown" or "angry" look (1 minute)
Step 63. Observe the cat's reaction to handling (5 minutes)
Step 64. Review the coat's resilience to touch (1 minute)
Step 65. Interview the current owner or breeder (30 minutes)
Step 66. Look for the lack of "oriental" features (2 minutes)
Step 67. Examine the shape of the paw pads (1 minute)
Step 68. Observe the cat from a distance (5 minutes)
Step 69. Check the ear set on the skull (1 minute)
Step 70. Look for a "cobby" but not "fat" appearance (2 minutes)
Step 71. Inspect the coat for any guard hairs (1 minute)
Step 72. Watch a video of British Shorthair standards (15 minutes)
Step 73. Check for the "stocky" leg structure (1 minute)
Step 74. Note the depth of the flanks (1 minute)
Step 75. Verify the cat's age (10 minutes)
Step 76. Look for the roundness of the top of the head (1 minute)
Step 77. Observe the nostril size (30 seconds)
Step 78. Finalize the coat color classification (5 minutes)
Step 79. Check the coat for a "crisp" break when the cat moves (1 minute)
Step 80. Observe the cat's play behavior (15 minutes)
Step 81. Check the pedigree for "Champion" lines (20 minutes)
Step 82. Evaluate the cat's overall balance (2 minutes)
Step 83. Inspect the ear base width (1 minute)
Step 84. Read a book on British Shorthair history (2 hours)
Step 85. Prepare the observation area (10 minutes)
Step 86. Examine the tail length relative to the torso (1 minute)
Step 87. Observe the cat's interaction with toys (10 minutes)
Step 88. Check for a "firm" feel to the body (1 minute)
Step 89. Compare the cat to a Chartreux (20 minutes)
Step 90. Observe the cat's grooming habits (15 minutes)
Step 91. Evaluate the muscle tone (5 minutes)
Step 92. Study the TICA breed standard (30 minutes)
Step 93. Clean the cat's coat for better inspection (10 minutes)
Step 94. Gather necessary measuring tools (5 minutes)
Step 95. Consult a second breed manual (45 minutes)
Step 96. Check for a "muff" on the cheeks (1 minute)
Step 97. Observe the cat in different lighting (10 minutes)
Step 98. Examine the coat for "ticking" (2 minutes)
Step 99. Check the density of the fur on the tail (1 minute)
Step 100. Wake the cat up for evaluation (1 minute)
